chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The one in Ihram slaughters the cow, the camel, and the sheep, and whatever does not array its wings from the birds, and whatever is permissible for the one not in Ihram to slaughter inside the Haram, so it is also permissible for the one in Ihram (to slaughter) in the unrestricted area as well as in the Haram.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.يَصُفَّ: To array its wings (specific type of bird)

ai.seo_question: What animals can a pilgrim in Ihram slaughter inside the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of slaughtering sacrificial animals (Hady) within the Haram boundaries while in the state of Ihram, affirming that the standard permissible livestock—cattle, camels, and sheep—as well as specific birds, may be slaughtered there. It underscores the continuity of the pilgrim's ritual obligations with general halal slaughter rules, a key point in Shia fiqh regarding the logistics of Hajj sacrifices. The ruling highlights the flexibility granted to pilgrims to perform the slaughter within the sacred precincts without invalidating their Ihram status.
